guide.title: Orphea's Overview
guide.text:
Orphea is an odd caster with above-average survivability and high damage
output potential but limited access to crowd control.
Given that all of Orphea's Abilities have a cast time or delay, they can all be
avoided by prepared opponents... unless you are better prepared.

guide.title: Orphea's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Powerful burst damage
High sustain damage potential for a caster
Excellent waveclear
Great follow up capacities
Relatively high survivability
Weaknesses
All Abilities have a short cast time or delay, making them avoidable
Very limited access to crowd control
Relatively short range on most Abilities
Unable to efficiently claim Mercenary Camps
Easy to counter, as the main healing source can be countered by having blinds or physical armor
Particularly weak when playing from behind

guide.title: Orphea's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Orphea synergizes with
Since Orphea depends highly on skillshots to deal damage, she works
well with any Hero that can provide reliable crowd control.
Her frailty also makes her dependent on other Heroes to peel for her
against melee Assassins particularly; Tanks tend to fulfill these
two needs, though other Hero types can too.
Orphea is countered by
Since Orphea relies heavily on skillshots with a
cast time to deal damage and on hitting her charged
Basic Attacks to heal herself, she is countered by many heroes. Her damage and
survivability can be significantly reduced by canceling her abilities, blinding
or evading her basic attacks, dashing out of her abilities, chaining
crowd control, or using very high range attacks.

guide.title: Orphea's Maps
guide.text:
Orphea's stronger maps
Orphea's average maps
Orphea's weaker maps
Orphea is a strong pick on snowball maps. She excels on maps with important bosses,
like Sky Temple and Tomb of the Spider Queen, because her
Eternal Feast is excellent in these situations. However,
her lack of single-target PvE damage makes her a poor choice
on maps like Battlefield of Eternity. As long as another hero can
claim Mercenary Camps, she remains a reasonable pick on most maps.

guide.title: Orphea's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Each enemy Hero hit by Overflowing Chaos generates one Chaos, making area hits key to improving your survivability.
Shadow Waltz may be tempting to use on-Cooldown, but using it to avoid dangerous skillshots is paramount.
Shadow Waltz does not require Orphea to instantly dash after hitting an enemy, the dash can be used after a delay to avoid a skillshot or to wait for her next ability to be ready.
Shadow Waltz's dash can be used to dodge certain player created walls, such as Leoric's Entomb or Tassadar's Force Wall.
Chomp synergises naturally with Shadow Waltz; use the latter to dash to your intended target.
Both Dread's initial wave and eruption can hit a given target, so it is better to aim slightly behind an immobilized or slowed target.
Before having Dead Magic, it is better to not waste Orphea's empowered Basic Attack on an armored enemy, as it would greatly reduce her healing output.
After reaching Level 20 with Crushing Jaws and picking Engulfing Oblivion, Orphea should not hesitate to use it on a tank enemy, as the -50 armor debuff is enough to burst anyone down.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Orphea's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Compared to most other casters, Orphea provides higher-than-average on-demand
burst damage and decent sustain damage. On the other hand, she lacks much
crowd control, making it necessary to pick her
along Heroes who can provide it. As with many Heroes who provide little more
than damage, Orphea's popularity depends entirely on her power level resulting
from game balance. Regardless, building a team composition that aims to stay
ahead of one's opponents in terms of Experience is the best way of exploiting
Orphea's strength as a snowballing Hero.
Due to her reliance on crowd control, Orphea is at her best when part of a
roaming group of Heroes. She can hold her own in the offlane as well against
most melee Heroes, but must be careful when rotating and
may need help clearing out large Mercenary Camps.

abilities.title: Shadow Waltz
abilities.text:
Shadow Waltz
(Q)
Orphea
Mana: 35
Cooldown: 5 seconds
After 0.5 seconds, deal 165 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in a line.
Hitting a Hero with Shadow Waltz sets its cooldown to 2 seconds, refunds 35 Mana, and causes Orphea to dash a short distance upon moving.
Shadow Waltz is Orphea's most important Ability. Shadow Waltz's short
Cooldown (2 seconds on Hero hits) gives it a high sustain damage output,
especially when considering Overflowing Chaos. Shadow Waltz's cooldown,
however, is significantly higher when failing to hit an enemy Hero (5 seconds).
This makes accuracy and the ability to follow up
on crowd control
important skills for Orphea players to develop.
Shadow Waltz's name comes from the short dashing effect that follows a
successful hit. This dashing effect can be triggered by right-clicking a point
or unit, upon which Orphea will rapidly move a short distance towards the
target. This effect can and should be used, as possible, to avoid enemy
skillshots or otherwise reposition yourself offensively for Basic Attacks
or Chomp. It should be noted that while Orphea can dash through units,
she cannot dash through terrain and Structures. However, she can move through
some walls generated by certain Heroes, such as Leoric's Entomb
or Tassadar's Force Wall.
Further, she cannot dash while under the effects of movement-preventing crowd
control.
Since Shadow Waltz has a 0.5 seconds cast time, care is required so as to
not miss one's intended target. In parallel, enemies are likely to try and
avoid Shadow Waltz due to its importance to Orphea, making mindgames an
important aspect of the Hero.
Although using Shadow Waltz on-Cooldown may be tempting, its utility in
avoiding dangerous Abilities makes restrained use much more prudent under most
circumstances.

abilities.title: Chomp
abilities.text:
Chomp
(W)
Orphea
Mana: 60
Cooldown: 10 seconds
After 0.625 seconds, deal 305 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies in front of Orphea.
Chomp is Orphea's highest damage Ability. Its very short range and relatively
long cast time, however, make it difficult to use on its own. This is why it is
generally preceded by an offensive Shadow Waltz's dash
to close the gap
between Orphea and the intended target. This combo is, in fact, the crux of
Orphea's offensive playstyle, particularly when following up
allied crowd control.
Chomp's area of effect is large enough to allow it to hit an entire Minion
wave, although its short range makes retaliation easy for opponents. In fact,
one should always be very mindful of their surroundings when using Chomp at any
time.

abilities.title: Dread
abilities.text:
Dread
(E)
Orphea
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 14 seconds
Release a wave of dread that deals 85 (+4% per level) damage to enemies hit. Dread erupts 0.75 seconds after reaching the end of its path, dealing 175 (+4% per level) damage. Enemies hit by Dread's wave or eruption are Slowed by 25% for 2 seconds.
Dread is Orphea's filler Ability. Its long range allows it to be lobbed at
immobile enemy Heroes and Minions alike safely and to good effect. Since Dread's
eruption effect has a short delay, it can be avoided by opponents. As such, you
should see to aim slightly ahead so as to force them to take the hit or fall
back and risk being hit by your other Abilities.
It should be noted that both Dread's initial wave and eruption can hit a
given target, making it optimal to aim slightly behind immobile targets (such
as those under the effects of crowd control) so as to
ensure double hits.
Further, Dread's eruption's Slow effect can help with hitting
Shadow Waltz and Chomp alike, as well as provide a limited means of
self-peeling.

abilities.title: Eternal Feast
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Eternal Feast
(R)
Orphea
Heroic
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 50 seconds
After 1.5 seconds, deal 210 (+4% per level) damage in an area. Eternal Feast repeats every 1 second as long as it hits an enemy Hero.
Eternal Feast is a large area of effect Ability designed specifically for
area denial. In other words, its purpose is to force enemies away from a
specific area of effect for fear that they may repeatedly trigger Eternal Feast.
Due to its long 1.5-second initial delay, hitting enemies with Eternal Feast
without the help of crowd control is unlikely. Without allied
crowd control to setup for it,
Eternal Feast is generally used to break
team fights apart or on important points of contention such as Objectives
and Bosses.

abilities.title: Crushing Jaws
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Crushing Jaws
(R)
Orphea
Heroic
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 70 seconds
After 1.25 seconds, pull enemies in an area towards the center, dealing 250 (+4% per level) damage and Stunning them for 0.5 seconds.
Crushing Jaws is Orphea's main team fighting Ability and only true source of
crowd control. Successful Crushing Jaws hits
allow you to follow up with
each of your other Abilities perfectly for significant amounts of damage. Your
allies, too, may find Crushing Jaws' effects useful to secure their own hits. As
such, you should aim to hit two or more Heroes, as possible. Beware, however, as
Crushing Jaws has a delay of 1.25 seconds, making it easy to avoid for Heroes
with a gap closer that is off-Cooldown. Crushing Jaws should certainly
be used in conjunction with allied crowd control so as to prevent it from being
avoided.
Crushing Jaws also opens up the possibility for Orphea to land solo kills
against some of the squishier Heroes, assuming it is
followed up with your other Abilities. Since Crushing Jaws has a relatively
short cooldown, this should be done whenever possible if you think you can
secure a kill.

abilities.title: Overflowing Chaos
abilities.text:
Overflowing Chaos
(D)
Orphea
Passive
Hitting an enemy Hero with a Basic Ability grants 1 Chaos. Chaos can stack up to 3 times.
While Orphea has Chaos, her Basic Attacks against Heroes consume all Chaos, dealing 50% increased damage per stack, and healing for 100% of the damage dealt.
Overflowing Chaos is Orphea's source of self sustain, and represents a
good reason to use Basic Attacks as often as possible, unlike most casters. To
maximise the use of Overflowing Chaos, one Basic Attack should be used against a
Hero every time 3 stacks are reached, as further stacks provide no additional
effect. Shadow Waltz can be used to help deal such Basic Attacks
and generally quickly generate Overflowing Chaos stacks.
It should be noted that hitting multiple Heroes with a single Basic Ability
cast does generate multiple Overflowing Chaos stacks, making area hits desirable
to try and land.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
En Pointe is for advanced players only, requiring a
whole build around it. It nearly doubles Shadow Waltz's damage,
but is hard to use reliably. Pick it only if you are very experienced with Orphea and
paired with Allegrissimo.
Growing Nightmare greatly increases Dread's
damage output even without quest completion. However, it should be chosen in very
specific cases as the eruption part of the ability is relatively easy to dodge.
It is very effective if you are focusing on following up
a tank from afar. It should only be chosen when paired with
Mind Devourer and Lurking Terror.
Ancestral Strength improves Orphea's damage output through its situational 15% damage
increase and modest but reliable Slow effect.
This effect makes each of Orphea's Abilities significantly
easier to hit to yield more damage and survivability.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Allegrissimo is a good option for this tier, boosting Orphea's
damage, mobility, and survivability. However, crowd control
easily cancels her Shadow Waltz, greatly reducing this talent's efficacy.
Therefore, it should only be chosen if enemies cannot
easily punish her; otherwise, Backbiter is a better choice.
Backbiter is overall a great talent, increasing your survivability
with 15% extra health and giving Orphea a new dash that can be used in several
ways. However, it shouldn't be paired with a Chomp-oriented build,
as the added dash will make it easier for enemies to kite her.
Chaotic Assault is a weak talent in the early game
and should only be picked when paired with Abyssal Symbiosis
at Level 13. Before that, Orphea will often attack without three stacks of
Overflowing Chaos, wasting this talent's potential.
However, after picking Abyssal Symbiosis, it will significantly increase her damage.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Insatiable provides a powerful cooldown reduction effect that can, in theory,
increase Chomp's damage output approximately four times.
In practice, this is rarely the case, but Insatiable still allows Orphea to become extremely
threatening at short range. It is only a good talent if enemies cannot easily
cancel your Chomp.
Ravenous Hunger is a difficult Quest with ultimately
limited payoff, particularly when considering
Insatiable's reliability as an alternative choice.
Mind Devourer is a versatile talent due to Dread's
uncancelable nature and large range. It can be picked in all games, and Orphea
should focus on completing it as soon as possible, as the cooldown reduction
after completion is excellent. Aiming Dread behind enemy
heroes to stack both the wave and eruption helps complete the quest quickly.

as a follow up, a peeling tool,
or for point control. The best way to use
this heroic is on an immobilized enemy to guarantee a significant portion
of the damage.
Crushing Jaws is a slow, short-range, high-cooldown,
and inconsistent heroic. It should only be picked if you need to cancel important
channeled abilities, like Mosh Pit
or Holy Word: Salvation. However, despite being a weak heroic ability,
it has an excellent upgrade at Level 20. It can be chosen for a late-game strategy
if you have allies that can help you land it.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Orphea
talent_pages.text:
✘︎
Determination
(Level 13)
Orphea
After dashing with Shadow Waltz, Orphea gains 50 Spell Armor against the next enemy Ability, stacking up to 2 times. While Orphea has Determination, her Physical damage is increased by 15%.
?
Abyssal Symbiosis
(Level 13)
Orphea
Hitting a Hero with Chomp instantly grants Orphea maximum Chaos and a 170 (+4% per level) Shield for 3 seconds.
✓
Invasive Miasma
(Level 13)
Orphea
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Activate to deal 150 (+4% per level) damage to all nearby enemies after 2 seconds. For each Hero hit, heal for 182 (+4% per level) and gain 1 Chaos.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Determination is a weak talent that provides minimal
resistance and a small damage boost that may not activate often.
Invasive Miasma usually offers more survivability,
damage, and waveclear, making it a much better choice at this talent tier.
Abyssal Symbiosis vastly increases Orphea's
survivability, making aggressive Chomp
usage safer and therefore more viable. Great synergy with Insatiable
and Chaotic Assault.
Invasive Miasma is the recommended option for this tier,
as it greatly increases her survivability, waveclear, and damage. It is not easy
to use and takes time to master due to its 2-second delay before activating.
However, if you are not used to it, activating it as soon as an enemy reaches
melee range is good choice, as the area will either make them retreat or greatly heal you.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Orphea
talent_pages.text:
?
Bond of Anguish
(Level 16)
Orphea
Shadow Waltz deals bonus damage to Heroes equal to 3% of their maximum Health, healing Orphea for 50% of damage dealt.
✓
Dead Magic
(Level 16)
Orphea
Basic Attacks that consume Chaos ignore Armor and deal 90 (+4% per level) Spell Damage to the target and all enemies around them.
?
Lurking Terror
(Level 16)
Orphea
Mana: 60
Cooldown: 10 seconds
After Dread erupts and for 2 seconds after, activate to cast Chomp from the eruption area. Enemy Heroes hit by this Chomp are Slowed by 70% for 1.5 seconds.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Bond of Anguish is only useful if you are using a full
Shadow Waltz build. In that case, it will greatly increase
Orphea's damage output and survivability. Otherwise, it should not be chosen.
Dead Magic significantly increases Orphea's
sustain damage output while being extremely simple to use.
It is particularly powerful against Heroes who rely on Armor, such as
Mal'Ganis, E.T.C. and Garrosh. The fact that it ignores
Armor also improves Orphea's self-sustain against
these targets, making it a very good quality-of-life improvement.
Lurking Terror should be chosen if your priority target
is a high-ranged backliner, where you cannot normally hit
Chomp. It is very consistent in these scenarios.
However, if enemies have high Armor, Dead Magic
should be picked instead.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Orphea
talent_pages.text:
✓
Monster Within
(Level 20)
Orphea
Eternal Feast grants 1 Chaos each time it hits a Hero. While Eternal Feast is active and for 5 seconds afterwards, Orphea's Basic Abilities recharge 150% faster.
?
Engulfing Oblivion
(Level 20)
Orphea
Crushing Jaws reduces the Armor of Heroes hit by 50 for 3 seconds. Takedowns set its cooldown to 5 seconds.
?
Eldritch Conduit
(Level 20)
Orphea
Each Chaos consumed increases Orphea's Spell Power by 3%, up to 30%. After reaching the maximum bonus, the Spell Power is increased by an additional 30%. Lasts 10 seconds.
?
Final Toccata
(Level 20)
Orphea
Cooldown: 20 seconds
Activate to instantly reset the cooldown of Shadow Waltz. For the next 5 seconds, dashing with Shadow Waltz resets its cooldown and increases the duration of Final Toccata by 1 second.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Monster Within is a good talent, excelling if you manage
to hit several targets with Eternal Feast. Even if it does
not hit any target, it remains valuable as it greatly reduces the downtime
between Orphea's combos due to the cooldown reduction it provides.
This makes it a good choice in most builds.
Engulfing Oblivion further empowers Orphea's signature
Crushing Jaws combo by not only increasing the ability's
damage but also bolstering allies'. Given that the heroic ability is very hard
to hit and reduces a significant amount of armor, it is a
good idea to aim for easy-to-hit targets. This allows you to burst down even
very healthy and tanky targets due to the -50 armor debuff.
Eldritch Conduit significantly boosts Orphea's damage
output, but it outperforms other options only if it frequently reaches maximum
stacks. This talent is best used in combination with
Abyssal Symbiosis, which makes stacking much easier.
Final Toccata is a good talent but is extremely weak
when not paired with Shadow Waltz talents. It is the
hardest talent to use in this tier, so it is only recommended for experienced
players. Additionally, it resets the Shadow Waltz
cooldown, so you can use it immediately if you miss a Q and need a quick recovery.
